title: Problem Decomposition
definition: Problem decomposition divides a bounded problem into smaller responsibilities whose inputs, outputs, and interactions can be reasoned about independently.
purpose: Turn a bounded problem into reviewable responsibilities without losing coverage or dependencies.
history: Decomposition and abstraction are foundational practices in computing, systems engineering, and software design.
mental_model: A decomposition tree shows responsibility ownership, while a dependency graph shows what each responsibility needs from others.
analogy: A team divides an event into venue, registration, safety, and communication responsibilities; the analogy fails if shared dependencies and feedback are hidden.
common_mistakes: Splitting only by file or technology layer
industry_notes: Clear responsibility and dependency boundaries improve planning, review, testability, and change isolation.
ai_notes: AI task decomposition must be checked for missing work, overlap, unsafe sequencing, and unverifiable completion criteria.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to decompose a bounded problem and defend the dependency order.
exercise_candidates: Repair a decomposition with overlap and missing responsibilities
lab_candidates: Create a decomposition tree and dependency graph
project_candidates: Map project responsibilities to acceptance criteria
